answers.answer: The State is the schema of the graph, meaning which keys exist, plus the reducer functions that specify how updates are applied to those keys. A node has the signature State -> Partial<State>: it reads the whole current state and returns a partial update rather than a replacement state.
accept: names the schema, or the set of keys, as one part
names reducers, or the rule for applying updates, as the other part
says a node returns a partial update rather than the whole state

answers.answer: The key holds only the third batch of documents. With no reducer attached, the default reducer ignores the left argument, meaning what is already in state, and replaces the state value with the right argument, meaning what the node returned. The first two retrievals are overwritten, and no error is raised because that is the documented default.
accept: says only the last write survives, or only the third batch remains
attributes it to the default reducer ignoring the left argument and replacing with the right one
notes that accumulation has to be requested explicitly rather than being the default

answers.answer: Concatenation would leave two entries for that message. add_messages merges the two lists by message id, so a message whose id already exists in state updates that existing entry instead of being appended as a duplicate; only messages with new ids are appended.
accept: says add_messages merges or matches on message id
says an existing message is updated in place rather than duplicated
says brand new messages are still appended

answers.answer: Edges decide what runs next; a node never names its successor. A node receives the current state, does the computation or side effect, and returns an updated state, which in practice is a partial update to the shared state.
accept: says edges, not nodes, determine control flow or the next node
says a node receives the current state and returns an update to it
makes clear the node does the work while the wiring is separate

answers.answer: add_conditional_edges wires it up. It takes the name of the node to route out of plus a routing function called after that node executes, and that function reads the state. When the passages are not good enough it returns the name of the retrieval node, sending control backwards so that node runs again; when they are good enough it returns 'END' and the graph stops.
accept: names add_conditional_edges
says the routing function is a function of the state and runs after the source node
says returning an earlier node name creates the loop
says returning 'END' terminates execution

answers.answer: StateGraph is a builder class and cannot be used directly for execution. Calling .compile() returns a separate executable graph, and that object is the one carrying invoke(), stream(), astream(), and ainvoke(). The wiring is fixed when the graph is compiled, so the runnable object is not the same value you added nodes and edges to.
accept: says StateGraph is a builder and cannot execute
names .compile() as what produces the runnable object
makes clear the assembled object and the run object are two different values

answers.answer: Record the version of the package the page was read against and the date it was read, because a documentation site serves the current release and will say something else later. A source file cited at a pinned commit can be retrieved exactly as quoted, so a reader can check the quote after the API has moved, while the unpinned documentation page cannot be recovered in the state it was read.
accept: names the version read against
names the retrieval date
says a pinned commit or permalink stays retrievable while the docs URL serves whatever is current
